en: The Apadāna of the Elder Kummāsadāyaka Naḷamāli Chapter 5 I gave a gift of tortoise meat to the Buddha, the Great Sage, who was seated upon a seat of grass. Because of that deed, I have attained the fruit of stream-entry; I am now a stream-enterer, no longer subject to rebirth in the lower realms. I shall attain parinirvāṇa before long. This is my final birth. I have reached the end of suffering. This is the Apadāna of the Elder Kummāsadāyaka.
“While the Great Seer Vipassi was wandering for alms,
I filled it with boiled rice.
when I gave that alms-food at that time;
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of the rice-mash.
The defilements have been burnt away by me.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
... [as before] ... the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā) have been attained.
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Kummāsadāyaka speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Kummāsadāyaka is the fifth.
